name: SJPW Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Won and lost twice across 1997 in a story the fed's own record tells almost entirely after the fact: Super Tengu took it from his rival Shinji Hamada in a pre-arranged finish at the fed's first pay-per-view, then dropped it to Ace Killcannon at the Super J Crown Tournament that September, with Derek Mota lined up for a cage-match challenge as the year closed.

name: SJPW All-Asian Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: SJPW's own top singles title, styled "All-Asian" rather than "World" to match the fed's regional self-presentation; the fed's own December 1997 record finds it vacant, with Nik Nyce and Shinji Hamada lined up to fill it following an unnamed former champion's forced retirement.
notes: No reign is dated from the two documents served this pass; the vacancy and the planned Nyce-Hamada match are the only holder information the surviving record gives (promotions/sjpw/archive/year-end-review-dec1997.html).

name: SJPW All-Asian Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Held by the end of 1997 by Black Sun Rising, the pairing of the underrated Blackline and the rookie Alex Akira -- the fed's own record gives no earlier holder or date for the belt.

name: SJPW Battle Arts Championship
epitaph: The title of SJPW's own smallest but hottest-drawing division, held by Steel Serpent as of the surviving record's end -- the fed's own account gives no earlier holder or date.

name: SJPW Middleweight Championship
epitaph: Settled by an SJPW-run tournament in which the favored rookie Jet Jaguar was upset in the finals by the underdog Ishikawa, per the fed's own account.

name: Gunryo Championship
epitaph: Held by Despair across the revival era's documented run, defended under its own named rules variant; no surviving document names an earlier holder or a title change.

name: NCWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Held for years by Masashi 'Lightning' Lanther before passing to Super Bakemono, who defended it successfully against El Santa Azteca in Okinawa in May 2004; no surviving document names the exact transition.

name: Grand Prix Heritage Championship
epitaph: A new singles championship first attested held by Kentaro "H-Bomb" Kawasaki in the documents immediately following the revival's own unread Zenmen Sensou supershow (26 June 2004), where a press conference had advance-announced a new title of this name; no document this pass could read records the title match itself.
